hints.title: Longest Palindromic Prefix Focus
hints.text: Adding characters in front to create a palindrome is equivalent to finding the longest prefix of s that is already a palindrome.

hints.title: Delimiter Converted String Invariant
hints.text: In the compound string s + "#" + rev(s), the longest prefix that matches a suffix corresponds precisely to the longest palindromic prefix of s.

hints.title: Prefix LPS Calculation Procedure
hints.text: Form combined string t = s + "#" + s[::-1]. Build the prefix array lps for t. The value lps[-1] yields the length k of the longest palindromic prefix in s. Prepend the reversed remaining suffix s[k:][::-1] to original string s.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def shortestPalindrome(self, s: str) -> str:
        rev = s[::-1]
        combo = s + '#' + rev
        n = len(combo)
        lps = [0] * n
        prev = 0
        i = 1
        while i < n:
            if combo[i] == combo[prev]:
                prev += 1
                lps[i] = prev
                i += 1
            elif prev > 0:
                prev = lps[prev - 1]
            else:
                lps[i] = 0
                i += 1
        k = lps[-1]
        return rev[:len(s) - k] + s
```

variables: N: input length or search state bound
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing all prefixes for palindrome symmetry naively takes O(N^2) time, hitting limits on 50,000-character inputs.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: KMP prefix array evaluation on the combined string runs in O(N) time with O(N) memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should convert the longest palindromic prefix problem into a KMP string matching problem via string reversal.
